title: Whipped Tallow Balm in Pineapple: I Tried Beef Fat on My Face
body:
Look. I know how this sounds. Beef fat. On your face. I get it. I was the same. My friend mentioned this tallow balm thing and I just stared at her. Like, tallow? The stuff from candles? Or cooking? For skin? It sounded like something from a weird homesteading blog, not a skincare routine. But my skin was being a real jerk last spring—flaky, tight, just generally unhappy—and I’d tried the expensive stuff from the fancy store in the mall. You know the one. It did nothing. So I was desperate. And curious. So I ordered this Whipped Tallow Balm in Pineapple from some little Etsy shop. I figured, worst case, I’m out thirty bucks and have a weird story.

Anyway. It showed up. Small jar. Cute label. I opened it.

## How I Started Putting Beef Tallow on My Face

I didn’t just slap it on. I was skeptical. I did a patch test on my wrist like a responsible adult, which I almost never do. Waited a day. Nothing happened. No rash. No weirdness. So I took a tiny bit. The texture was… not what I expected. It was whipped, like the name says. Not greasy. Not hard. Somewhere between butter and frosting? Cold when you scoop it, then it warms up on your fingers. I rubbed it between my palms and just… smelled it. Pineapple. But not like candy. Or a cleaner. It was like pineapple if a pineapple was on vacation and also very chill. Sweet, but not fake. A little bright. Cheerful. I don’t know how to describe smells. It was nice though.

So I put it on my face. At night. After washing. I braced for a greasy pillowcase situation.

It didn’t happen. The balm just… went away. My skin drank it. It left my face feeling soft, but not slick. Not sticky. Just normal. But better. Hydrated. I woke up and my skin wasn’t tight. It was calm. Weird. Good weird.

Here’s the thing I had to figure out: why would beef tallow for skin even work? It sounds so medieval. But then I read a little. And it’s not that crazy. Tallow, especially from grass-fed cows, is apparently really similar to the oils our own skin makes. Our sebum. So it’s like giving your skin something it already recognizes. It absorbs deep. It doesn’t just sit on top and pretend to do something. It’s not a synthetic barrier. It’s food. For your face. I know, I know. It still sounds odd. But when you think about slathering on a dozen unpronounceable chemicals from a lab, is this really weirder?

## What This Pineapple Tallow Balm Actually Does

It’s not magic. It’s just really good at one thing: moisturizing. Like, actually fixing dry skin. My hands get destroyed in spring. Wind, washing them a million times, whatever. They crack. I used this balm on my knuckles. The cracks healed faster. My elbows, which are always rough, got smooth. Like, actually smooth. I haven’t seen my elbows this smooth since… I don’t know when. Maybe never.

I started using it every night. Just a little scoop. The jar from that Etsy seller lasted forever. Months. And my skin just… stabilized. No more random dry patches. No more that tight feeling after a shower. My complexion even looked quieter. Less red. I have this one spot on my cheek that always gets irritated. It just… stopped.

I told my sister about it. She has eczema on her arms. She was horrified at first. “You put what on your face?” But she tried it. She texted me two weeks later like, “Okay. I hate that you were right.” Her patches calmed down. Not gone, but way less angry. She said it was the only thing that didn’t sting.

That’s the other part. It’s simple. The ingredient list is short. Tallow, some oils, essential oils for the pineapple scent. That’s it. No fragrance cocktails, no preservatives with sixteen syllables. For sensitive skin, that’s a big deal. It’s just less stuff for your skin to fight with.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

So it’s been a while now. I’m on my second jar. I keep it on my nightstand. It’s part of the routine. Brush teeth, wash face, tallow balm. Done.

The mental hurdle is gone. I don’t think “beef fat” anymore. I think “that balm that works.” It’s just a cream to me now. A cream that happens to be made from tallow. A cream that smells like a tropical escape in a jar, which is a nice bonus when it’s raining for the tenth day in a row in April.

I compared it to that hundred-dollar cream I bought before. The fancy one in the heavy glass jar. That one felt nice going on, sure. Silky. But an hour later, my skin would feel tight again. It was all show. This tallow balm? No show. All results. It’s humble. It’s not trying to be luxurious. It just is.

And the scent. God, the scent. The Pineapple one is so good. It’s not overpowering. It doesn’t linger all night. It’s just this little burst of happy when you open the jar. Summer vibes. Vacation feeling. It makes the whole thing feel less like a medical treatment and more like a tiny, cheerful ritual. I look forward to it.

## Would I Buy This Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. Obviously. I already did.

I even got one for my mom. She’s into natural stuff. She loved it. Uses it on her cuticles.

For anyone wondering “is tallow good for skin” based on my totally non-expert, just-a-person experience… yeah. For me, it is. It fixed a problem nothing else would. The benefits of a tallow balm, for me, were real hydration that lasts, calming my sensitive skin, and just… simplicity.

It’s not for everyone. If the idea totally skeeves you out, you won’t get past it. And that’s fine. But if you’re curious, and your skin is being difficult, and you’re tired of products that promise the world and deliver a pamphlet… it might be worth a shot. I’m glad I got past the weirdness. My skin is happier. I’m happier. That’s the whole point, right?

Anyway. That’s my take. I don’t know what else to say.

---

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
For a lot of people, yeah. It sounds wild, but it’s structurally similar to the oils our skin makes naturally. So it absorbs really well and helps repair the skin barrier. It’s an old-school remedy that’s having a moment again for a reason.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
It hasn’t for me, and I can get clogged pores easy. Because it’s so similar to our own sebum, it seems to sink in instead of sitting on top and blocking things. It’s non-comedogenic. But everyone’s skin is different, so a patch test is always smart.

**What does the Pineapple tallow balm smell like?**
It smells like actual pineapple, but not in a sugary candy way. More like the fruit itself—sweet, bright, a little tropical. It’s cheerful. The scent is from essential oils, and it’s not super strong. It fades pretty quickly after you put it on.
